lead_headline: Weekend restaurant tracker logs 5 new leads—Vaultaire's HiFi lounge opens beneath La Forêt, Super Mega Bien shuts after 8 years, Aspen Baking collapses mid-acquisition

restaurant.blurb: 5 new leads since Friday lift active count to 58 total (29 openings, 29 closures)—opening-closure parity tightest in weeks. Weekend openings: Vaultaire's subterranean HiFi bar debuts Wednesday beneath La Forêt (Speer), FiNO Mediterranean launches soft opening Tuesday at All Inn Hotel (City Park), Wash Park Social replaces Grille today. Closure side: Super Mega Bien shutters March 14 (Five Points, 8-year RiNo staple cited financial pressures), Aspen Baking Company ceases operations March 6 mid-acquisition (Stapleton wholesaler's sudden collapse strands restaurant clients), Your Mom's House seized for taxes (Capitol Hill venue's December auction). Geographic clustering persists: Union Station captures four weekend openings (Mendocino Farms Highland debut, Ogo Korean BBQ, GQue BBQ expansion, C Burger), Regis logs three closures (303 Ramen fire damage, dual Dairy Queen exits). Lead quality remains high—confidence scores average 9/10.

foreclosure.blurb: 42 new filings this week—up 40% from prior week's 30—mark sharpest weekly jump since late January, shattering March's early calm. 104 auctions queue next seven days, but $71M total exposure compresses as mega-filing drought persists: only one $795K Weld County case crosses seven figures. $57M Arapahoe outlier (2038 S Vaughn) skews aggregate but signals commercial distress, not residential volume surge. County standings: El Paso leads 475 active, Weld climbs to 431, Arapahoe holds 451. March volatility intensifies—30-to-72 filing weekly swings replace January's steady 50+ baseline as predictable rhythm fractures into boom-bust cadence. Seven-day acceleration suggests distress wave building, not data noise.

reputation.blurb: 49 mentions past seven days across 10 sources—up 14% from prior week's 43, reversing two-week decline. Denver Post dominates with 23 pickups (47% share), social platforms deliver 13 (Instagram 9, Facebook 4), Hoodline contributes 4. Weekend highlights: Post's lawsuit/tax archive pages, Facebook's Denver REIT $5B IPO valuation story, Hoodline's Kwame Spearman/Denver Book Society breakup coverage. Source concentration tightens: Post plus social command 73% of weekly volume—single-outlet dependency remains structural vulnerability as niche publishers contribute sporadically. Discovery stays 100% Google News RSS. Monthly pace: 135 mentions through 23 days projects 181-mention March if sustained, tracking 40% above February's final count.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +3 since Friday (4 new, 1 canceled) pushes MTD to +34 (+1.5/day), 90-day cumulative to +104 (+1.2/day). Weekend acquisition modest but consistent—Friday logged +3, Saturday/Sunday flat—typical weekend lull after weekday gains. Seven-day window: +15 net (21 new, 6 canceled) trails prior week's +21 but sustains March's elevated pace: month's 1.5/day rate runs 15% above YTD's 1.3/day benchmark. Recent fortnight shows stabilization: new subscriber flow normalizes at 3-4 daily baseline post-March 9's 8-new spike, cancellation floor compresses to 0.9/day vs March average of 1.4/day. Pattern: three-week consolidation after early-month churn, acquisition steadies, retention improves. March on track for strongest monthly net gain year-to-date.
